subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student who believes 'my exam results depend mostly on my own effort and preparation' has what psychologists call an internal:
explanation: Internal locus of control means a person attributes outcomes mainly to their own effort/actions, while external locus of control attributes outcomes to luck, fate, or other external factors — internal locus is generally linked to higher motivation and achievement.

subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student who fails a test and says 'I just didn't try hard enough this time, I'll do better next time with more preparation' is making an attribution to a cause that is:
explanation: Weiner's attribution theory classifies causes along three dimensions: locus (internal/external), stability (stable/unstable), and controllability. Attributing failure to 'not trying hard enough' is an internal, unstable, controllable cause (effort) — the most motivationally productive attribution, since it implies improvement is possible.
